audits.text:
## 50385c1a773f

**Reproduced semantic shortcut — actionable.** Generator SHA-256 `1cdc0b6058f3d8e57a26fb0bc9c41028f9c176e87b7b9b6c375366f5e7c577a5` declares `EXAMPLES_NEEDED = 3` but no `strict_canonical_like`, `SEMANTIC_WITNESSES`, or `lesson_identifiable` contract; the strict audit semantic gate fails for that reason (`checks/audit/50385c1a773f/stage-audit/`).

The omission produces an actual ambiguous window. On `difficulty=easy`, `seed=0`, start index `7`, the three demonstrations all terminate at gray walls and the following query exits the boundary with two unused wall components. The concrete `wall_only` rival applies the canonical painting to wall-terminated inputs but returns boundary-exit inputs unchanged. It matches all three demonstrations and differs on the query, whose canonical path contains 11 black cells. The deterministic probe checked 1,200 windows per band and found **108 such wall/wall/wall → boundary windows in each band**. Reproducer and fingerprints: `checks/audit/50385c1a773f/window_probe.py` and `checks/audit/50385c1a773f/window_probe.log`.

A second QA defect compounds this: the retained tests use legacy staged imports and a fixed `__file__.parents[...]` root, so the portable audit reports a missing canonical path before semantic testing. No source was modified in this audit.
